_source: Ministry of Education / Curriculum Development Centre, Zambia — English Scheme of Work, Form 2, Terms 1 and 2 merged (Term 3 was not found in either Drive folder). Each entry cites the syllabus page it is drawn from. The source document's teacher name and school name have been removed — this file contains no identifying information about who prepared the source scheme, per this app's standing content policy of crediting only CDC/Ministry of Education. As with english_form1.json, this scheme teaches by spaced repetition: Listening & Speaking, Comprehension, Composition and Summary Writing each largely repeat their Term 1 sub-topics again in Term 2 (with two genuinely new Listening & Speaking sub-topics, Clarifications and Figurative Language) while Structure continues introducing new grammar content nearly every week across both terms. Sub-topics are listed once, at their first appearance across either term; competencies/learning objectives are merged where the same sub-topic gained a genuinely new specific-competence code in Term 2 (e.g. 2.4.5 Comparison). Mid-term test and end-of-term test/revision weeks carry no new topic content and are omitted.

subject.name: English Language
subject.description: Ordinary Level Secondary English Language syllabus, Form 1-4 (Curriculum Development Centre).

grade.name: Form 2
grade.phase: Secondary — the source scheme itself uses "Form 2" for this level under the 2023 CBC.

terms.name: Terms 1 and 2 (taught as a continuous, repeating cycle — see _source; Term 3 was not found)

sub_topics.name: 2.1.1 Instructions
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: instructions given and received appropriately.

competencies.description: Give and receive instructions

learning_objectives.description: Discussing situations where instructions are given/received and using appropriate language to sequence them (Firstly, Secondly, Next, Lastly)
Role-playing following of instructions given

sub_topics.name: 2.1.2 Directions
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: directions given and received appropriately.

competencies.description: Give and receive directions

learning_objectives.description: Discussing situations where directions are given/received and identifying direction vocabulary (left, right, adjacent to, beyond, underneath)
Role-playing giving and getting directions

sub_topics.name: 2.1.3 Announcements
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: language to make announcements used correctly.

competencies.description: Use appropriate language to make announcements

learning_objectives.description: Discussing appropriate language for announcements (clear, concise, objective tone) and reacting to announcements
Role-playing making and responding to announcements

sub_topics.name: 2.1.4 Expressing Emotions
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: appropriate language to express sympathy used correctly.

competencies.description: Use appropriate language to express sympathy

learning_objectives.description: Discussing situations for expressing sympathy and identifying sympathy language (My condolences, I am here for you)
Practising expressing sympathy in different situations

sub_topics.name: 2.1.5 Compliments
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: language to compliment others used correctly.

competencies.description: Use appropriate language to compliment others

learning_objectives.description: Identifying achievements/occasions requiring compliments and discussing compliment vocabulary (Congratulations!, Well done!)
Role-playing giving and receiving compliments

sub_topics.name: 2.1.6 Greetings
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: language to greet different categories of people used appropriately.

competencies.description: Use appropriate language to greet different categories of people

learning_objectives.description: Discussing ways of greeting the young/peers (formal/informal) and adults/elderly people
Role-playing greeting different categories of people

sub_topics.name: 2.1.7 Public Speaking
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: appropriate language to debate used correctly.

competencies.description: Use appropriate language to debate

learning_objectives.description: Identifying situations necessitating a debate and using appropriate debating language (I have a dissenting view, In my opinion)
Holding debates on cross-cutting issues (Climate Change, Corruption, Human Rights)

sub_topics.name: 2.1.8 Invitations
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: language to invite people used appropriately.

competencies.description: Use appropriate language to invite people

learning_objectives.description: Identifying situations requiring invitations and discussing invitation vocabulary
Role-playing inviting people to different occasions

sub_topics.name: 2.1.9 Conversations
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: language to initiate conversations, make offers and make requests used appropriately.

competencies.description: Use appropriate language to initiate conversations
Use appropriate language to make an offer
Use appropriate language to make requests

learning_objectives.description: Discussing how to initiate conversations and role-playing
Identifying situations requiring an offer and practising making an offer through role-play
Discussing language used to make a request and role-playing making a request

sub_topics.name: 2.1.10 Clarifications
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: language used to seek clarification used appropriately.

competencies.description: Use appropriate language to seek clarification

learning_objectives.description: Discussing language used to seek clarification (Would you mind explaining what you mean?)
Role-playing seeking clarification

sub_topics.name: 2.1.11 Figurative Language
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: figurative language used appropriately.

competencies.description: Use figures of speech in various social contexts

learning_objectives.description: Discussing figures of speech (riddles, proverbs, idioms, similes, metaphor, euphemism)
Using figurative language in conversation

sub_topics.name: 2.2.1 Listening Comprehension
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: listening to oral sources and answering questions done effectively. Revisited repeatedly across the term.

competencies.description: Listen to different oral sources of information and answer questions

learning_objectives.description: Listening to different oral sources (radio, television, someone speaking) and answering different types of questions
Identifying and listing main ideas (note-taking) and retelling information

sub_topics.name: 2.2.2 Reading Passages Efficiently
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: passages read efficiently. Revisited repeatedly across the term.

competencies.description: Read passages efficiently

learning_objectives.description: Reading at a speed of 250 words per minute; skimming and scanning
Answering factual and inference questions, retelling details, and deducing meanings of unfamiliar words and idiomatic expressions

sub_topics.name: 2.2.3 Reading Unabridged Materials
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: different unabridged materials read. Revisited repeatedly across the term.

competencies.description: Read different unabridged materials for enjoyment

learning_objectives.description: Reading a variety of texts (newspapers, magazines, journals) silently and at an appropriate pace
Reading critically and making discriminating judgements (theme, characterisation, style, setting)

sub_topics.name: 2.3.1 Narratives
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: stories written appropriately.

competencies.description: Write stories

learning_objectives.description: Discussing features/techniques of narratives (plot, setting, characterisation, conflict, point of view, resolution)
Writing narratives based on given situations

sub_topics.name: 2.3.2 Descriptive Writing
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: a place described correctly.

competencies.description: Describe a place

learning_objectives.description: Discussing adjectives and language appealing to the five senses to describe a place
Using descriptive techniques (naming, detailing, comparison) to write descriptive compositions

sub_topics.name: 2.3.3 Report Writing
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: a simple report written correctly.

competencies.description: Write a simple report

learning_objectives.description: Identifying types of reports (police, book, school, incident-based) and discussing features (title, past tense, formal language, factual)
Answering WH questions and writing simple reports from given notes

sub_topics.name: 2.3.4 Speech Writing
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: a speech of introduction written correctly.

competencies.description: Write a speech of introduction

learning_objectives.description: Identifying types of speeches and discussing features of a speech of introduction (protocol, background, purpose)
Composing and giving a speech of introduction orally

sub_topics.name: 2.3.5 Biography Writing
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: an auto-biography and a biography written accordingly.

competencies.description: Write an auto-biography
Write a biography

learning_objectives.description: Discussing an auto-biography, its types (semi, fictional), structure and features (1st person, DOB, place of birth), and writing one
Discussing the purpose, structure (3rd person, life story) and features of a biography, and writing one

sub_topics.name: 2.3.6 Expository Writing
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: expository composition written correctly.

competencies.description: Write an expository composition

learning_objectives.description: Discussing features of an expository composition (clear purpose, objective tone, formal language)
Making an outline of points and writing expository compositions on cross-cutting issues (Financial Education, HIV/AIDS)

sub_topics.name: 2.3.7 Persuasive Writing
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: an argumentative and a discursive composition written correctly/appropriately.

competencies.description: Write an argumentative composition
Write a discursive composition

learning_objectives.description: Discussing features of argumentative writing (picking a side, evidence-based) and using language to agree/disagree with controversial statements
Discussing features of a discursive composition (formal/objective tone, both sides discussed), researching, and writing

sub_topics.name: 2.3.8 Diary Writing
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: diary entries written correctly.

competencies.description: Write diary entries

learning_objectives.description: Discussing features (date, time, note form, 1st person, brevity) and structure/format of a diary
Writing diary entries based on given notes

sub_topics.name: 2.3.9 Letter Writing
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: a semi-formal letter written correctly.

competencies.description: Write a semi-formal letter

learning_objectives.description: Identifying the purpose of semi-formal letters (apologising to a neighbour, writing to civic leaders) and outlining their layout
Writing a semi-formal letter on a given situation

sub_topics.name: 2.4.1 Tenses
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: the emphatic form of future tense and the unreal past used in sentences correctly.

competencies.description: Use the emphatic form of the future tense in sentences
Use the unreal past in sentences

learning_objectives.description: Discussing the use of the emphatic 'shall' (firm resolve/determination) and constructing sentences
Discussing the unreal past (not referring to actual past time) and using it to construct sentences

sub_topics.name: 2.4.2 Verb Expressions
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: verbs and expressions followed by -ing, object + infinitive, and the infinitive used correctly in sentences.

competencies.description: Use verbs and expressions followed by -ing in sentences
Use verbs followed by object + infinitive in sentences
Use verbs followed by the Infinitive in sentences

learning_objectives.description: Discussing the pattern verb + -ing (enjoy, avoid, finish, stop) and expression + -ing (can't help, can't stand)
Discussing the pattern verb + object + infinitive (advise, allow, instruct, remind)
Discussing the pattern verb + to + verb (agree, decide, refuse, forget)

sub_topics.name: 2.4.3 Determiners
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: adjectives of quantity, possessive adjectives and demonstrative adjectives used correctly in sentences.

competencies.description: Use adjectives of quantity in sentences
Use possessive adjectives as determiners in sentences
Use demonstrative adjectives in sentences

learning_objectives.description: Discussing adjectives that show quantity (some, all, much, little, enough)
Discussing adjectives showing possession (my, your, his, her, its, our, their)
Discussing words that demonstrate and introduce the noun (this, these, that, those) and their position

sub_topics.name: 2.4.4 Relative Clauses
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: relative pronouns, and defining/non-defining relative clauses, used correctly in sentences.

competencies.description: Construct sentences using relative pronouns
Use defining and non-defining relative clauses in sentences

learning_objectives.description: Identifying different relative pronouns (which, whom, that) and discussing subject/object in sentence construction
Discussing relative pronouns that introduce a relative clause and distinguishing defining from non-defining clauses

sub_topics.name: 2.4.5 Comparison
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: comparatives, superlatives, and alternative/parallel-increase comparison structures used correctly in sentences.

competencies.description: Use comparatives and superlatives in sentences
Use alternative ways of expressing comparison (similes, as...as, the same...as)
Use parallel increase (the + comparative and the + comparative) to express comparison

learning_objectives.description: Discussing ways of comparing two things (comparative, -er/more) and more than two things (superlative, -est/most)
Discussing irregular forms and constructing sentences

sub_topics.name: 2.4.6 Reason
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: 'now that'/'seeing that' and participial phrases to express reason used correctly in sentences.

competencies.description: Use 'now that'/'seeing that' to express reason in sentences
Use Participial Phrases to express reason in sentences

learning_objectives.description: Discussing the use of 'now that'/'seeing that' to express reason
Discussing the formation and use of participial phrases to express reason

sub_topics.name: 2.4.7 Time
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: expressions of time used correctly.

competencies.description: Use expressions of time

learning_objectives.description: Using phrases with the Perfect Participle (Having completed) and conjunction + participial phrases to express time
Using 'no sooner...than' with inversion as an alternative to 'as soon as'

sub_topics.name: 2.4.8 Contrast
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: other expressions to show contrast in sentences used correctly.

competencies.description: Use other expressions to show contrast in sentences

learning_objectives.description: Using present participle with 'despite'/'in spite of' for contrast
Using 'one...the other', 'no matter...', adjective + as/though

sub_topics.name: 2.4.9 Condition
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: other ways of expressing condition used correctly.

competencies.description: Use other ways of expressing condition

learning_objectives.description: Discussing 'but for' and 'if only' to show condition
Using 'provided/providing that', 'so/as long as', 'supposing that', and composing sentences showing inversion in conditional sentences

sub_topics.name: 2.4.10 Question Tags
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: question tags used correctly.

competencies.description: Use question tags

learning_objectives.description: Identifying the use of question tags in speech and discussing positive/negative tag rules and imperative statement tags
Supplying correct question tags to given statements

sub_topics.name: 2.4.11 Voice
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: active and passive voice used correctly.

competencies.description: Use the active and passive voice

learning_objectives.description: Using active voice when the subject performs the action and passive voice when the subject receives the action

sub_topics.name: 2.4.12 Agreement (Concord)
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: subject-verb agreement used correctly.

competencies.description: Use subject-verb agreement

learning_objectives.description: Discussing subject-verb agreement rules and constructing sentences expressing correct subject-verb agreement

sub_topics.name: 2.4.13 Word Building (Affixation)
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: affixation to form new words used correctly.

competencies.description: Use affixation to form new words

learning_objectives.description: Discussing the process of adding prefixes/suffixes to form new words and identifying various prefixes and suffixes (en, dis, un, pre; er, tion, al)
Forming new words using affixation

sub_topics.name: 2.5.1 Title Summary
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: titles composed correctly. Revisited repeatedly across the term.

competencies.description: Compose titles

learning_objectives.description: Choosing best titles from options given on a passage and composing titles from a given passage

sub_topics.name: 2.5.2 Sentence Summary
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: sentence summaries composed correctly. Revisited repeatedly across the term.

competencies.description: Compose sentence summaries

learning_objectives.description: Identifying the main idea or claim in a sentence and summarising it in a shorter form while maintaining meaning

sub_topics.name: 2.5.3 Paragraph Summary
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: paragraph summaries composed correctly. Revisited repeatedly across the term.

competencies.description: Compose paragraph summaries

learning_objectives.description: Identifying main ideas and supporting details in a paragraph, omitting unnecessary information, and paraphrasing

sub_topics.name: 2.5.4 Tabulation Skills
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: tabulation skills to summarise information applied correctly. Revisited repeatedly across the term.

competencies.description: Apply tabulation skills to summarise information

learning_objectives.description: Identifying and categorising information, and creating tables, charts and graphs to organise data

sub_topics.name: 2.5.5 Abbreviations
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: abbreviations to take or make notes used correctly.

competencies.description: Use abbreviations to take or make notes

learning_objectives.description: Discussing types of abbreviations (initialisms, blends, clips, acronyms) and using them when taking notes

sub_topics.name: 2.5.6 Verbal Summaries
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: information summarised orally correctly.

competencies.description: Summarise information orally

learning_objectives.description: Identifying main ideas and key points, organising them logically, and summarising a short text/conversation orally in own words

sub_topics.name: 2.5.7 Prose Summaries
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: prose summaries written correctly.

competencies.description: Write prose summaries

learning_objectives.description: Identifying main and supporting ideas, distinguishing fact from opinion, and writing concise, clear prose summaries
